messages:
nora: Heads-up: hit a reproducible SSE chunk-merge when doing immediate reconnects in the new sampleapp (v0.10). This is with node-sdk@1.4.0 and python-sdk@0.8 behaving slightly differently.

nora: Steps: start stream -> ctrl-c within 100-300ms of first data -> reconnect immediately. Sometimes the next event arrives with the trailing line from the previous connection appended to the new event's data field.

nora: Raw capture from tcpdump (abbreviated):
```
--- conn A last bytes ---
data: {"part":"hello
"}

--- conn B first bytes ---
data: {"part":"world"}

# observed merged on some runs:
data: {"part":"hello
"}
data: {"part":"world"}
# but parsed by node-sdk as a single data event: {"part":"hello
"}
{"part":"world"}
```

ash: was the socket closed cleanly (FIN) or aborted (RST)? that affects stream boundary detection.

nora: seems like CLOSE (FIN) most times, but sometimes we see no FIN before new connection (client closed process -> kernel race).

ash: which parser lib are each SDKs using? node's low-level parser tends to coalesce chunks if you don't explicitly flush on "end"/"close". python aiohttp seems to create separate events more reliably.

kevin: I ran quick local runs: node-sdk parser keeps an internal buffer and only emits on blank-line delimiter. If the previous connection closes while there's data without a trailing blank line, buffer persists until next delim, so next bytes get appended. Not ideal.

ash: two quick fixes: (1) on socket close/error, force-emit or drop partial buffer; (2) treat an incoming `event:` or `id:` line with no preceding blank-line as start-of-new-event (i.e., implicit delimiter). Both are small and complementary.

nora: implemented (1) in my branch: parser.on('close', () => parser._flushPartial(true)); where _flushPartial(true) will emit partial as its own data event with a comment about truncated. That fixed the merge in 90% of my runs.

kevin: nice. for parity, please port to python-sdk too — the aiohttp client needs explicit _drain on connection close to avoid leaving bytes in transport buffer.

ash: also add a test that simulates the kernel-level race: spawn child that connects, sends "data: {..}" without trailing blank line, exit immediately, then create a new connection and send next event. CI can run this fast with loopback.

nora: created issue DEVEX-2041 with repro harness and logs. devex-bot created it automatically.

devex-bot: Created issue DEVEX-2041: "sse: partial event buffer survives client reconnect -> merged data events" (link: https://tracker.internal/DEVEX-2041)

kevin: small caution: emitting truncated partial events may change semantic counting for some consumers (they expect well-formed JSON in data). Better to emit a special "__partial_truncated" meta or emit as comment line so downstream JSON parsing won't choke.

nora: good point. For now we emit a comment prefix `:partial-truncated` then the partial payload, so it's not valid JSON and parsers that expect JSON will ignore it unless they handle comments. Also added a flag to opt-in to aggressive flush in SDK constructor.

ash: can you paste the node change? I'll review.

nora: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/node-sdk/pull/812 - key patch: in sse-parser.js add `socket.on('close', () => { if (parser.buffer.length) { parser.emit('comment', 'partial-truncated'); parser.emit('data', parser.buffer); parser.reset(); } });` plus unit test.

kevin: LGTM-ish. please add an integration test hitting the sampleapp endpoint to ensure sampleapp updated to v0.10 includes parser reset. Also update docs/streaming.md to mention immediate-reconnect edge-case and the opt-in behavior.

ash: will coordinate backport. which releases do we want? 1.4.x and 1.3.x?

nora: target: patch to 1.4.1 and 1.3.5. sampleapp pinned to node-sdk 1.3 in some demos so backport important.

kevin: another follow-up: consider a server-side fix too. If backend writes each event followed by double newline and then `\n` flush, it's less likely to merge. But can't rely on all backends. Server-side suggestion: add `\n` after each event and optionally send `retry:` comment between connections.

nora: agreed. I patched sample backend to always flush with `\n` and that reduced incidence but didn't eliminate it under fast reconnect. So client-side remains necessary.

ash: ok. I'll merge after CI and then cut patch release. Thanks for catching this before the external demo.

nora: thanks team. I'll post a short note in docs and sampleapp changelog once releases are cut.
